ID: Nice Intro to Tai Chi for Older Learners
Content: I did a little bit of Tai Chi a decade or more ago, and always wanted to get back into it. I found this set and figured I'd try it. I really like it because it's a routine that you don't have to think about. The instructor David tells you what to do. He's very level and even-keel throughout the videos. The nice thing is that after a few minutes, you can start feeling it. It's nice to help center your mind, slow your breathing, and get a little fitter in the process.

The nice thing is that after a few minutes, you can start feeling it. It's nice to help center your mind, slow your breathing, and get a little fitter in the process.

There are various 'forms' or movement patterns, and in this set, you don't have to learn the patterns because you're following the instructor. If you continue learning Tai Chi, you can dig into the various forms and learn them, but like I said, this is a great place to start.

This is a fun set for anyone, not just the fifty plus set. The instructor is clear and the routines are easy to follow. You will definitely feel better after doing them. Very low pressure and relaxed but remarkably effective. My mother had a stroke and the seated program is perfect for her. She just started the balance dvd too. Moving has helped her physically and mentally.
